selection.viewer_promise: Understand how a visible score becomes a governed decision.

selection.why_competing_genre_loses: The payoff is the governance mechanism, not a product verdict, comparison, or buying decision.

narrative_map.pain_point: A fluent answer can sound certain even when the model is guessing.
narrative_map.hook: A fluent answer can sound certain even when the model is guessing. Jev takes a different route: typed probabilities for a bounded decision.
narrative_map.open_loop: The Short makes the operator work visible: inspect the score, apply the policy, retain human ownership, and preserve the receipt.
narrative_map.frame: A score is an input to a governed decision; policy, ownership, and retained evidence determine what happens next.
narrative_map.practitioner_proof: In the evaluation harness I have been building, typed probabilities make the real work visible; the harness remains mock-qualified and live provider use remains on hold.
explanatory_progression: Inspect the score and distinguish a 0.81 result from a 0.54 result.
Apply a pre-authorized policy to route, review, or stop the bounded decision.
Keep exceptions and irreversible actions with a person, then retain the versioned receipt.
narrative_map.practical_value: Operators can see the score, threshold, owner, and evidence behind the handoff.
narrative_map.cta: Use the approved field guide as a review test: ask what threshold applies, who owns the exception, and which receipt remains before a score moves work.
narrative_map.closing_principle: Governed automation begins when uncertainty is visible enough to route, review, and refuse.
narrative_map.conclusion: Governed automation begins when uncertainty is visible enough to route, review, and refuse.
narrative_map.channel_cta: Subscribe to the channel for more practical ways to govern AI decisions.

script.text: A fluent answer can sound certain even when the model is guessing. Jev takes a different route: typed probabilities for a bounded decision. In the evaluation harness I have been building, that makes the real work visible. First, inspect the score. A 0.81 result can route differently from one at 0.54. Then apply a pre-authorized policy: route, review, or stop. Finally, keep exceptions and irreversible actions with a person, and retain the versioned receipt. The value is practical: operators can see the score, the threshold, the owner, and the evidence behind the handoff. Jev’s launch does not prove production reliability, and my current harness remains mock-qualified with live provider use on hold. Use the field guide as a review test. Before any score moves work, ask what threshold applies, who owns the exception, and which receipt remains. Governed automation begins when uncertainty is visible enough to route, review, and refuse. Subscribe to the channel for more practical ways to govern AI decisions.
